stem: Best guess: a charity earns dividends on its endowment. Is that income taxable?

choices.text: Yes, as unrelated business taxable income
No, unless the stock is debt-financed
choices.explanation: Correct. §512(b)(1) excludes dividends, interest, and similar passive income.

choices.text: Yes, at the trust tax rates

choices.explanation: The $1,000 threshold is for filing Form 990-T.

explanation: §512(b)(1) excludes dividends, interest, and similar passive income.

stem: A public charity has gross receipts of $150,000 and total assets of $600,000. Which annual return is it eligible to file?

choices.explanation: Correct. 990-EZ requires receipts under $200,000 AND assets under $500,000.

explanation: 990-EZ requires receipts under $200,000 AND assets under $500,000.

stem: Which activity of a §501(c)(3) school generates UBTI?

choices.text: Renting its stadium, with staff and catering, to a pro team
choices.explanation: Correct. Rent with significant services and a regularly carried-on, unrelated business is UBTI.

choices.text: A campus bookstore selling textbooks to students
Interest earned on its bank deposits
A bake sale staffed entirely by volunteers

explanation: Rent with significant services and a regularly carried-on, unrelated business is UBTI.

stem: When is Form 990 due for a calendar-year 2025 organization (no extension)?

choices.explanation: That's for individuals, C corporations, and trusts.
Correct. 15th day of the 5th month after year-end.
The due date is the 15th day of the 5th month.

explanation: 15th day of the 5th month after year-end.

stem: What happens to an organization that doesn't file its required annual return for 3 consecutive years?

choices.text: Nothing, if it has no UBTI

choices.explanation: Correct. §6033(j): automatic revocation after 3 consecutive years of not filing.

explanation: §6033(j): automatic revocation after 3 consecutive years of not filing.

stem: An exempt organization has two unrelated businesses: A earns $50,000 and B loses $(20,000). Before the specific deduction, what is UBTI?

choices.explanation: Correct. §512(a)(6): each unrelated trade or business is computed separately; B's loss carries forward for B.
The silo rule prevents netting between businesses.

explanation: §512(a)(6): each unrelated trade or business is computed separately; B's loss carries forward for B.

stem: Which organization pays a 1.39% excise tax on its net investment income?

choices.explanation: Public charities don't pay the §4940 tax.
Correct. §4940: 1.39% of net investment income for private foundations.

explanation: §4940: 1.39% of net investment income for private foundations.

stem: A charity's gross UBI is $1,500 with $300 of directly connected expenses. What is taxable UBTI and must it file Form 990-T?

choices.explanation: Gross UBI of $1,000 or more requires filing.
Subtracts the deduction from gross UBI and misses the filing test.

explanation: Form 990-T is required when gross UBI is $1,000 or more; UBTI = 1,500 − 300 − 1,000 = 200.

stem: A charity's executive (a disqualified person) receives $80,000 above reasonable compensation. What is the initial excise tax on the executive?
explanation: §4958: 25% first-tier tax on the excess benefit.

stem: Which revenue is a qualified sponsorship payment excluded from UBTI?

choices.text: A company pays a charity to run its ads, with pricing and endorsements, in the charity's magazine
A company buys the charity's mailing list
choices.explanation: List rentals are generally UBTI except among exempt organizations.

choices.text: A company pays for exclusive sales rights at a stadium
A company pays to have its name and logo displayed at a charity run, with no qualitative claims
choices.explanation: Correct. §513(i): acknowledgment of the sponsor's name/logo without advertising is excluded.

explanation: §513(i): acknowledgment of the sponsor's name/logo without advertising is excluded.

stem: An organization wants its §501(c)(3) exemption to be retroactive to its formation date. By when must it generally file Form 1023?

choices.explanation: Correct. Filed within 27 months (15 months + automatic 12-month extension), exemption is retroactive to formation.

explanation: Filed within 27 months (15 months + automatic 12-month extension), exemption is retroactive to formation.

stem: A charity rents part of its building (average acquisition debt $200,000; average adjusted basis $800,000) for net rent of $60,000. How much is UBTI before the specific deduction?
A §501(c)(3) organization endorses a candidate for public office. What is the consequence?

choices.explanation: Political campaign activity is prohibited outright.
Correct. §501(c)(3) organizations are absolutely prohibited from political campaign activity.

choices.text: Nothing, if the endorsement is unpaid

explanation: §501(c)(3) organizations are absolutely prohibited from political campaign activity.

stem: A §501(c)(3) runs a thrift shop staffed entirely by volunteers. Is its income UBTI?
explanation: A trade or business in which substantially all the work is done by unpaid volunteers isn't an unrelated trade or business.

stem: Which income of an exempt organization is generally excluded from UBTI?

choices.text: Income from a public restaurant it runs

choices.explanation: Correct. Passive investment income is excluded.

explanation: Dividends, interest, royalties and most real-property rents are excluded, unless debt-financed.

stem: An exempt organization has $1,200 of gross unrelated business income. Must it file Form 990-T?

choices.explanation: Correct. Filing depends on gross UBI.

choices.text: Only if it owes tax on the UBTI

explanation: Form 990-T is required when gross unrelated business income is $1,000 or more.

stem: A private foundation's minimum distribution amount is $500,000, but it distributes only $300,000 by the deadline. What is the initial excise tax?
explanation: §4942 imposes an initial 30% tax on a private foundation's undistributed income.

stem: A private foundation leases office space from its founder at fair rent. How is the lease treated?

choices.text: As self-dealing, even at fair rent
choices.explanation: Correct. Leasing with a disqualified person is self-dealing.

choices.text: As allowed because the rent is fair

explanation: §4941: leasing property between a private foundation and a disqualified person is self-dealing regardless of fairness (with narrow exceptions).

stem: A university licenses its name and logo to an apparel maker for royalties, with no active involvement. Is the royalty income UBTI?

choices.text: Yes, it's a trade or business

explanation: Royalties are excluded from UBTI unless debt-financed or from a controlled entity.

stem: An exempt organization rents out a building with furniture; the furniture rent is 30% of the total. How is the rent treated?

choices.explanation: Personal property rent over 10% is taxable.

choices.text: All of the rent is UBTI
Only the furniture rent is UBTI
choices.explanation: Correct. Personal property rent between 10% and 50% is taxable.

choices.text: Only the building rent is UBTI

explanation: Personal property rent is excluded only if incidental (10% or less). From 10% to 50%, the personal property portion is UBTI; above 50%, all the rent is UBTI.

stem: A private foundation and its disqualified persons together own 35% of a business's voting stock. What issue arises?

choices.explanation: Correct. Combined holdings generally can't exceed 20%.

explanation: §4943 generally limits a foundation and its disqualified persons to 20% of a business's voting stock.

stem: An exempt organization is a limited partner in a partnership that runs an unrelated business. What is the effect?

choices.text: Its share of business income is UBTI

explanation: An exempt partner's share of partnership income from an unrelated trade or business is UBTI.

stem: When is Form 990-T due for a calendar-year exempt corporation, without extension?

choices.explanation: Correct. The 15th day of the 5th month.

explanation: Exempt corporations file Form 990-T by the 15th day of the 5th month after year-end.

stem: A university runs a bookstore selling textbooks mainly to its students. Is the bookstore's income UBTI?

choices.text: Yes, retail sales are always UBTI

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.
Correct. Businesses run mainly for members' or students' convenience are excluded.

explanation: The convenience exception covers a §501(c)(3) college's trade or business carried on mainly for its students.

stem: A charity conducts bingo games that are legal under state and local law. How is the income treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. A specific bingo exception applies.

choices.text: Taxable only if run by volunteers

explanation: Income from bingo games legal under state and local law is excluded from UBTI.

stem: A private foundation awards travel grants to individuals without IRS-approved selection procedures. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Correct. Grants to individuals need advance approval of procedures.

explanation: §4945: grants to individuals for travel or study are taxable expenditures unless made under IRS-approved procedures.

stem: What excise tax rate applies to a private foundation's net investment income?
explanation: Private foundations pay a 1.39% excise tax on net investment income.

stem: What minimum annual distribution must a private nonoperating foundation make?
explanation: Private nonoperating foundations must distribute about 5% of noncharitable-use assets each year.

stem: What excise tax applies to an exempt organization's compensation over $1 million to a covered employee?
explanation: A 21% excise tax applies to remuneration over $1 million and excess parachute payments.

stem: An exempt organization has $50,000 of unrelated trade income and $20,000 of directly connected expenses. It's a corporation. What is the UBIT?
explanation: UBTI is reduced by the $1,000 specific deduction and taxed at corporate rates.

stem: An exempt organization has two unrelated businesses: A earns $30,000, and B loses $20,000. What is UBTI?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses can't offset other trades.

explanation: Under §512(a)(6), each unrelated trade is computed separately.

stem: A charity owns a $1,000,000 rental building with $400,000 of average acquisition debt. Net rental income is $100,000. How much is UBTI?
explanation: Debt-financed income is taxable in proportion to average acquisition debt over basis.

stem: An exempt organization earns dividends, interest and royalties. Are they UBTI?
explanation: Dividends, interest, royalties and most rents are excluded from UBTI unless debt-financed or from controlled entities.

stem: A charity runs a thrift shop staffed entirely by volunteers. Is the income UBTI?

choices.explanation: Correct. Substantially all work is unpaid.

explanation: Businesses with substantially all work done by unpaid volunteers are excluded.

stem: A university runs a bookstore mainly for its students. Is the income UBTI?
explanation: Businesses carried on mainly for the convenience of members, students or employees are excluded.

stem: A company pays a charity $50,000 for a logo acknowledgment, with no comparative or qualitative claims. Is it UBTI?
explanation: Qualified sponsorship payments for acknowledgment only aren't UBTI; advertising is.

stem: A foundation manager sells land to the foundation for $100,000. What first-tier tax applies to the self-dealer?
explanation: Self-dealing triggers a 10% first-tier tax on the disqualified person.

stem: A private foundation fails to distribute $200,000 of required income. What initial tax applies?
explanation: A 30% initial tax applies to undistributed income not distributed by the deadline.

stem: A foundation and its disqualified persons together own 25% of a business's voting stock. What limit is exceeded?
explanation: Combined holdings above 20% of voting stock are generally excess business holdings.

stem: A charity has $900,000 of total support, of which $350,000 counts as public support. How is it likely classified?
explanation: Organizations normally receiving at least one-third of support from the public are publicly supported charities.

stem: A charity that made the §501(h) election exceeds its lobbying limit. What applies?

choices.explanation: Correct. Revocation risk if far over.

explanation: Electing charities pay 25% excise on excess lobbying expenditures.

stem: An exempt hospital pays its CEO $1,500,000 in 2025. What excise tax does the hospital owe?
explanation: The excise tax applies to remuneration over $1 million.

stem: A private foundation has $500,000 of net investment income. What excise tax applies?
explanation: Private foundations pay 1.39% of net investment income.

stem: An exempt organization's new venture loses money while another unrelated business is profitable. What is the tax effect?
explanation: Losses from one unrelated trade can't offset income from another.

stem: A charity plans to borrow to buy a rental building. What should it consider?

choices.explanation: Correct. Part of the rent becomes UBTI.

explanation: Debt-financed property income is taxable in proportion to acquisition debt.

stem: A charity wants corporate sponsorship income without UBIT. What should the sponsor receive?
explanation: Acknowledgments with logos are fine; qualitative or comparative claims make it advertising.

stem: A family foundation's trustee wants to buy property from the founder at fair value. What is the issue?

choices.explanation: Not this rule in this case.

explanation: Most transactions between a private foundation and disqualified persons are self-dealing regardless of price.

stem: A new charity depends on a few large donors. What classification risk does it face?

choices.explanation: Correct. It may fail the public support test.

explanation: Charities relying on a few large donors may fail the public support test and become private foundations.

stem: An exempt organization plans a major lobbying campaign. What could help it manage the limits?
explanation: The §501(h) election replaces the vague substantial-part test with defined spending limits.

stem: A private foundation's investment income is rising sharply. What ongoing obligation grows with assets?
explanation: Higher asset values increase the minimum distribution required of private nonoperating foundations.
